system.name: Sabre
system.one_liner: a hardware-accelerated snapshot compression system for serverless microVMs using Intel IAA

components.name: Guest physical memory
components.role: guest memory pages (yellow = dirty), compressed on creation and reconstructed on restore

components.name: Huffman tables
components.role: per-chunk compression statistics used to Huffman-encode dirty pages

components.name: Compressed partitions
components.role: IAA-compressed chunks of dirty memory written to the snapshot file

components.name: snapshot file
components.role: on-disk file holding the compressed partitions

components.name: mem pool
components.role: optional pre-allocated buffer pool used during decompression

components.name: userfaultd
components.role: installs decompressed pages into guest memory via user-space page faults

components.name: Partitions
components.role: decompressed partition data read from the partition file

content.key_idea: Sabre creates compressed VM snapshots using Intel IAA hardware, then restores memory either by prefetching one contiguous decompressed chunk via userfaultfd or by scattering decompressed partitions directly into memory with DMA.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three lettered panels: (A) how a snapshot is compressed, (B) single-chunk prefetching into guest memory, (C) scattered direct-DMA prefetching.

encoding.color_means: yellow marks dirty (modified) guest memory pages; dark red/maroon marks compressed or partitioned data structures; gray marks non-dirty pages and generic UI chrome

evidence: Figure 7-A shows an overview of Sabre's snapshot creation pipeline along with two designs for memory prefetching
Sabre also implements memory prefetching based on scattered IAA decompression (Figure 7-C)
Sabre directly DMAs decompressed partitions into the right locations in the guest's physical memory

summary: Figure 7 compares Sabre's three hardware-accelerated snapshot mechanisms for serverless microVMs, drawn as three lettered side-by-side pipelines sharing a common visual vocabulary. Panel (A) shows snapshot creation: guest physical memory (dirty pages in yellow) is run through an IAA statistics pass to build Huffman tables and an IAA Huffman pass to produce compressed partitions, which are written to a snapshot file alongside a partition file. Panel (B) shows single-chunk prefetching: the snapshot file is mmap'd and decompressed as one contiguous IAA operation (optionally through a memory pool) while the partition file's partitions are read separately, and userfaultfd installs the result into guest memory. Panel (C) shows scattered prefetching: the same inputs are instead decompressed and DMA'd directly into their scattered destinations in guest memory, bypassing userfaultfd. Yellow marks dirty pages and dark red marks compressed/partitioned data structures throughout.
summary_zh: 该图用三个字母面板对比 Sabre 的快照压缩与两种预取：(A) 用 IAA 统计与霍夫曼编码生成压缩分区；(B) 单块预取经 userfaultfd 写回；(C) 分散预取直接 DMA 写入。
notes: layout-proposal: triptych-pipeline-comparison — three side-by-side lettered (A/B/C) mini-pipelines sharing a common visual vocabulary (files, IAA stages, guest-memory bar) to compare snapshot creation against two prefetching strategies; the index's panels=1 (single image) is kept per the schema even though the figure reads as three sub-diagrams.
